Q: Thanks for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this
call?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please describe where you were when the collision happened.
A: I was on the highway in Sugar Land, in the right lane, heading toward the exit. Traffic had slowed a little, so I
moved over into the middle lane to get around a trcuk that was merging.
Q: Did you check your mirrors and blind spot before you changed lanes?
A: I checked the mirror and I glanced over my shoulder. I didn't see anyone right beside me, so I signaled and started
moving over.
Q: What happened next?
A: About halfway into the lane, I felt a bump and heard scraping on my passenger side. A gray sedan had come up
alongside me and our cars sideswiped each other. I pulled onto the shoulder right away.
Q: Did you notice the other vehicle before the impact?
A: No, not until it was right there. I don't think it was in my mirror when I looked.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. I put my left hand out to brace against the steering wheel and my wrist took most of the force. It swelled up
quickly and I could barely move my fingers. An ambulance took me to the hospital, where they told me the wrist was
fractured and I'd need a cast and follow-up with a specialist.
Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I have a follow-up appointment next week and I'm wearing a splint most of the day. I've also missed some
work because I can't drive comfortably or use my left hand for much.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm sorry the accident happened and I hope the other driver is alright.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
</page>
